scheme_name: Providing Latest Technology to Group of Pottery Artisans (Energy Efficient Kiln)
description:
The scheme titled "Providing Latest Technology to Group of Pottery Artisans (Energy Efficient Kiln)" was launched by the Government of India in 2021. 

This initiative aims to support pottery artisans by upgrading their kilns to energy-efficient models. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to enhance the productivity of pottery artisans while reducing energy consumption. 

The government has set a measurable target of upgrading at least 1,000 kilns across various states within the first two years of the scheme's implementation. 

This initiative is part of a broader effort to promote sustainable practices in traditional crafts and improve the livelihoods of artisans. 

The scheme specifically focuses on providing financial assistance to groups of pottery artisans. 

Each group can receive a subsidy of up to 50 percent of the total cost of the energy-efficient kiln. 

The maximum subsidy amount is capped at ₹1 lakh per kiln. 

This means that if a kiln costs ₹2 lakh, the artisans would need to contribute ₹1 lakh, while the government would provide the remaining ₹1 lakh. 

The energy-efficient kilns are designed to reduce fuel consumption by approximately 30 to 40 percent compared to traditional kilns. 

This reduction in fuel use not only lowers operational costs for artisans but also minimizes environmental impact. 

The scheme is particularly beneficial for artisans who are part of cooperatives or self-help groups. 

Eligibility criteria for the scheme include being a registered pottery artisan or a member of a recognized artisan group. 

Artisans must also demonstrate a history of pottery production and must be engaged in the craft for at least three years. 

The income limit for eligibility is set at ₹3 lakh per annum for individual artisans. 

For groups, the combined income of all members should not exceed ₹15 lakh per annum. 

The application process involves several steps. 

First, interested artisans must form a group of at least 10 members. 

Next, they need to register their group with the relevant state department of handicrafts. 

Once registered, the group must submit an application for the scheme along with the required documents. 

Required documents include proof of identity for all members, proof of income, and a detailed project report outlining the need for the kiln. 

The project report should include cost estimates and the expected benefits of upgrading to an energy-efficient kiln. 

After submission, the application will be reviewed by the state handicrafts department. 

If approved, the artisans will receive a sanction letter detailing the subsidy amount. 

The artisans are then required to procure the kiln from a government-approved vendor. 

Once the kiln is installed, artisans must submit proof of installation to receive the subsidy. 

The disbursement of the subsidy is typically processed within 30 days of receiving the installation proof. 

The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Textiles in collaboration with the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises. 

State handicrafts departments play a crucial role in the ground-level implementation of the scheme. 

They are responsible for conducting awareness programs and assisting artisans in the application process. 

The government has allocated ₹50 crores for the initial phase of this scheme. 

This funding is intended to cover the costs of subsidies for the first 1,000 kilns. 

The scheme is expected to create approximately 5,000 direct and indirect jobs in the pottery sector. 

Artisans are encouraged to adopt modern techniques and sustainable practices through this initiative. 

The energy-efficient kilns are designed to be user-friendly and require minimal training for artisans to operate. 

The scheme also aims to reduce the carbon footprint associated with pottery production. 

By adopting these kilns, artisans can contribute to national goals of reducing greenhouse gas emissions. 

The government has emphasized the importance of preserving traditional crafts while promoting modernization. 

Artisans who upgrade their kilns are likely to see an increase in their production capacity. 

This can lead to higher income levels and improved living standards for their families. 

The scheme also aligns with the "Make in India" initiative, promoting local craftsmanship. 

In addition to energy efficiency, the new kilns are designed to improve the quality of pottery produced. 

This can enhance marketability and open up new avenues for artisans to sell their products. 

The government is also exploring partnerships with NGOs and private organizations to expand the reach of the scheme. 

These partnerships can provide additional resources and training for artisans. 

Feedback mechanisms have been established to assess the impact of the scheme on artisan communities. 

Regular monitoring and evaluation will help in making necessary adjustments to the program. 

Artisans are encouraged to share their experiences and challenges faced during the implementation of the scheme. 

This feedback will be crucial for future iterations of the program. 

The scheme is part of a larger framework of support for traditional artisans in India. 

It complements other initiatives aimed at skill development and financial inclusion. 

The government aims to create a holistic ecosystem for artisans to thrive in a competitive market. 

As of October 2023, the scheme continues to receive positive responses from the pottery community. 

Artisans have reported significant improvements in their production efficiency and cost savings. 

The initiative has also sparked interest in energy-efficient technologies among other artisan groups. 

Overall, the "Providing Latest Technology to Group of Pottery Artisans (Energy Efficient Kiln)" scheme represents a significant step towards modernizing traditional crafts while ensuring sustainability. 

The government remains committed to supporting artisans through innovative solutions and financial assistance. 

This scheme is a testament to the importance of preserving cultural heritage while embracing technological advancements. 

Artisans are encouraged to stay informed about the scheme and participate actively. 

The future of pottery artisans in India looks promising with the support of such initiatives.
